items.title: Ray Bauduc and Nappy Lamare Interview, 1959-09-09
items.q: And he sort of inspired me a little. And also this banjo player with the Rhythm Kings. I don't remember his name. Louis Black.

ctx.x: Do you remember him? I never got to know him. I imagine there was some kid on a boat, a colored kid, played a real fine banjo. I don't even remember his name. And he sort of inspired me a little. And also this banjo player with the Rhythm Kings. I don't remember his name. Louis Black. Louis Black. Oh, yeah. In Chicago. Yeah. He played wonderful. Yeah, well, that's...

I listened to him on those records. There's one thing I wanted to ask Ray was telling us the other night, if we don't take all your intermission either, but a little bit about the... a little bit about the two beat, like we were talking about down beat again, and the Crosby period saying that all Dixieland is two beat rhythm. And you were explaining the other night that that's the wrong idea. Oh, well, it isn't the wrong idea.
